summary: An announcement for the first phase of the October 1971 Network Working Group meeting: a hands-on workshop at MIT's Project MAC for system programmers whose sites had working Telnet. Teams would test the network from MAC consoles to find remaining problems. Attendance was capped at about a dozen people.

eli5.summary: A call for a small group of computer experts to gather and try out the network together, poking at it to find what is broken. Only about twelve people could come.

sections.title: The Workshop Invitation
sections.content:
As described in RFC 207 and RFC 212, the next ARPA Network Working Group meeting is at MIT Project MAC in Cambridge, Massachusetts, October 10 to 14, 1971. Its first phase is a workshop for system programmers from sites with operational TELNET interfaces.

No more than a dozen system programmers should attend. They should know protocols, their own NCPs and their TELNET implementations. Sites send a name to Anne Speare by telephone.
sections.eli5: Before the big meeting, a small team of experts is invited to test the network together. Only about twelve can come.

sections.title: How the Workshop Runs
sections.content:
The workshop starts at noon on Sunday, October 10 with a strategy meeting in Project MAC's second floor conference room, #217. The first mission is to establish and exercise all possible TELNET connections with MAC's PDP-10 (Host 70). Teams then pair up, nesting TELNETs, to fill in the matrix of possible TELNET connections.

Teams work from MAC consoles until late Monday evening. Participants expect to find and fix implementation problems, discuss protocol and get an introduction to a wide variety of hosts.
sections.eli5: First everybody tries to connect to one computer. Then they pair up and try every connection between every pair until the whole chart is filled in.

sections.title: Preparation and Follow-up
sections.content:
MIT is preparing documentation on its user TELNET and a site-use scenario booklet, and wants advice from participating hosts. It hopes to establish routine usage with as many sites as possible before the workshop, is working to stabilize its system and is arranging on-site hardware repair staff.

It hopes knowledgeable network people will be on call at the sites to fix minor problems on the fly. The workshop experience will be an input to the NWG sessions that follow, including specific reports for the protocol review and status sessions.
sections.eli5: Hosts get ready, with repair people nearby and experts on call, so the test goes smoothly. What they learn goes into reports for the big meeting.
